# Results — Study 203 (Golden-Butterfly) on real daily data

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The Golden Butterfly
(20% SPY / 20% IWN / 20% TLT / 20% SHY / 20% GLD, annually rebalanced) vs 100%
SPY, 60/40 (SPY/TLT), and the Permanent Portfolio 25/25/25/25 (Study 144). As-of
**2026-06-15**; prices from a per-study yfinance cache (``_cache/gb_panel.parquet``,
``auto_adjust=True`` — dividends and splits folded in — total-return series). GLD
incepted 2004-11-18, bounding the joint window. Rebalance cost: 1 bp one-way.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Role | Window |
|---|---|---|
| SPY | US large-cap blend (total return) | 2004-11-18 to 2026-06-15 |
| IWN | US small-cap value (total return) | 2004-11-18 to 2026-06-15 |
| TLT | Long Treasuries 20y+ (total return) | 2004-11-18 to 2026-06-15 |
| SHY | Short Treasuries / cash proxy (total return) | 2004-11-18 to 2026-06-15 |
| GLD | Gold (total return incl. expense ratio) | 2004-11-18 to 2026-06-15 |

Panel fingerprint: `e00a60d52c6f` (sha1 of all five price vectors)

## Headline stats — annual rebalance, 1 bp one-way cost

| Portfolio | CAGR | Vol | Sharpe (ex-SHY) | Max DD | Worst Year |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **GB 20/20/20/20/20** | **7.78%** | **8.74%** | **0.682** | **−19.3%** | **−13.8%** |
| PP 25/25/25/25 | 7.44% | 7.39% | 0.782 | −18.4% | −13.5% |
| 60/40 SPY/TLT | 8.64% | 10.54% | 0.657 | −27.6% | −23.4% |
| 100% SPY | 10.99% | 18.92% | 0.532 | −55.2% | −36.8% |

The GB **trails on CAGR** by 3.2 pp vs SPY and 0.9 pp vs 60/40 over the
21-year window. Vs the Permanent Portfolio, the GB earns **+0.34 pp/yr more
CAGR** but has slightly higher vol (8.74% vs 7.39%) and slightly lower Sharpe
(0.682 vs 0.782), because the small-cap-value leg (IWN) adds return variance
without proportionally adding the regime-protection the PP's long-bond
concentration provides.

**The GB does not meaningfully improve on the PP**. The small-cap-value premium
boosted CAGR modestly, but the PP has a higher Sharpe and similar max drawdown.

## Inference

### HAC t-stats on annual return differences (GB minus benchmark)

| Comparison | HAC t (annual) | Interpretation |
|---|--:|---|
| GB minus SPY | **−1.82** | GB earns significantly less — the return forfeiture is real |
| GB minus PP | **+0.65** | Insignificant; GB barely edges PP on raw return |
| GB minus 60/40 | **−0.85** | Insignificant return gap; 60/40 edges GB on raw CAGR |

*Newey-West HAC on 22 annual return differences; negative = GB earns less.*

### Bootstrap Sharpe difference (GB minus benchmark, excess-of-SHY)

| Comparison | Point est. | 95% CI | GB wins resamples |
|---|--:|---|--:|
| GB vs SPY | **+0.150** | [−0.096, +0.387] | **88%** |
| GB vs PP | **−0.100** | [−0.289, +0.101] | **16%** |
| GB vs 60/40 | **+0.026** | [−0.193, +0.235] | **60%** |

*Circular block bootstrap (block=21 days, n=2000, seed=203). The GB vs SPY
Sharpe gap is directionally robust (88% win rate) but CI spans zero.
**The GB vs PP comparison reverses sign**: the PP wins 84% of bootstrap
resamples on Sharpe, evidence that the fifth leg (small-cap value) does not
improve the risk-adjusted profile over the Permanent Portfolio in this window.*

## Regime performance — SPY drawdowns >10%

| Episode | SPY | IWN | TLT | GLD | SHY |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2007-10 to 2009-03 (GFC) | −55.2% | −59.5% | +25.1% | +23.9% | +8.9% |
| 2015-07 to 2016-02 | −13.0% | −19.4% | +14.8% | +12.6% | +0.7% |
| 2018-01 to 2018-02 | −10.1% | −8.8% | −3.8% | −2.4% | −0.0% |
| 2018-09 to 2018-12 | −19.3% | −24.2% | +4.5% | +5.0% | +1.2% |
| 2020-02 to 2020-03 (COVID) | −33.7% | −43.1% | +14.2% | −3.6% | +2.1% |
| 2022-01 to 2022-10 | −24.5% | −20.6% | −29.3% | −7.3% | −4.4% |
| 2025-02 to 2025-04 | −18.8% | −20.9% | +0.8% | +1.6% | +1.3% |

**Key finding:** IWN amplifies the equity drawdown in 6 of 7 crash episodes.
In the GFC (2008), IWN fell −59.5% vs SPY's −55.2%. In COVID (2020), IWN
fell −43.1% vs SPY's −33.7%. The small-cap-value leg is a *return enhancer*
in bull markets but a *drawdown amplifier* in crashes — the opposite of what
the defensive legs (TLT, GLD, SHY) do. This directly explains why the GB's
max drawdown (−19.3%) is worse than the PP's (−18.4%) despite having a higher
equity allocation spread.

but it concentrates losses in the worst equity drawdowns.

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL (risk-adjusted vs SPY, conditionally).** GB Sharpe 0.682 vs
  0.532 (SPY); bootstrap 95% CI [−0.096, +0.387]; GB wins 88% of resamples.
  The Sharpe advantage vs SPY is directionally robust but **not certified at 5%**.
  **Against the PP, the GB loses on Sharpe (0.682 vs 0.782)**: the fifth leg
  adds return variance without proportional regime protection. Signal graded as
  REAL on the defensive dimension vs SPY, but WEAK vs the PP comparison.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** Five liquid ETFs, annual rebalance, <1 bp CAGR
  cost impact. Structurally fragile because: (a) the small-cap-value premium is
  well-documented but has had significant multi-year drawdown periods; (b) the
  2004-2021 bond+gold bull inflates the Sharpe (same caveat as the PP); (c) IWN
  amplifies equity drawdowns, which cuts against the portfolio's defensive
  marketing. A disciplined investor can hold it; the behavioural hurdle is
  watching IWN lag in the years right before it outperforms.
